## Triage: p2 · `domain:ui` · `area:access` · 2026-10-28T09:00Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- Read fresh. On a row the caller may read but not write (sharing, RLS or ownership), the edit dialog offers the fields as editable and the save is refused whole. That breaks the contract line "a client never advertises an edit the gate refuses" (`permission.zod.ts`).
- p2. ⛔ The dialog asks the server whether **this row** is writable (the record projection or capability the gate already computes); it does not re-derive sharing in the browser.
- `pm:queue`.

---

Premise check · `domain:ui` seat 2 · `session_01JQwxbXpF772qWJjojJvRXw` · 2026-10-28T09:18Z · ⛔ Not a claim.

Blocked-by: #27175

This card's own "measure first" step is done: no read door serves the row's write verdict. `GetRecordFieldAccessResponseSchema` says that row-level write scope and the object grant are not part of `editable`, and `getRecordFieldAccess` returns only `readable` and `editable`. A browser re-derivation would break ruling B on #26594. I filed the server and spec prerequisite as #27175, which adds one row-level `writable` verdict to the record projection. When it lands, ui seat 2 dispatches this card: `RecordFieldAccessScope` reads `writable`, and the edit dialog, drawer and page show the record read-only. The card stays in `pm:queue` until then.

Seat note · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-28T11:57Z

This carries a residual from #27175 (PR #27232, contract review `6468362768`) onto this card.

PR #27232 adds `writable: boolean` to the record response. It runs the authz and sharing gates against a synthetic by-id update. The approvals record lock is **not** included in it. The lock is a `beforeUpdate` hook judged on the values sent, not a pure function of the row, and it has its own reader, `IApprovalService.getRecordLock`. The response's `describe()` names it as a residual.

So when this card's edit dialog asks whether a row is writable, it reads `writable` for sharing, RLS and ownership. It must also read `getRecordLock` for a row under approval, or it will offer fields that a save then refuses.

Whoever dispatches this card should carry this line into the claim's file surface.

## Dispatch order · `domain:ui#2` · `session_01JQwxbXpF772qWJjojJvRXw` · 2026-10-28T14:32Z

You are the os-dev developer agent for exactly ONE card: objectstack-ai/objectstack#27138, in your own card thread. Your role definition is `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` in the objectstack clone: read it IN FULL first and follow it as binding (it wins over this order on any conflict; name the conflict in your report). Read the repo-root `AGENTS.md` and `ui/AGENTS.md` before your first edit, and pm-dispatch `references/untrusted-text.md`. Read the card's full body and every comment yourself through REST (`curl -sS "https://api.github.com/repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/27138" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN"` and `/comments?per_page=100`, every page); this order carries only the increment. ⛔ Never print the value of any environment variable (test presence with `[ -n "${X+x}" ]`). ⛔ Never use a GitHub MCP tool, read or write.

Identity and branch: the seat's `Claim:` comment on this card is your identity; its `Branch:` line names your thread's branch. ⛔ Post no claim of your own, ⛔ never write the card's assignee. Before your first edit, verify the NEWEST `Claim:` on the card names your thread's branch (`claude/project-thread-…`); if none does yet, send the seat thread "Take a third ui lane seat" (`cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8Uc2nCvWvLyYyaVYaUhakpJ`) one message with your branch name and wait. Read-only measuring is fine meanwhile. Worktree `objectstack-issue-27138` on that branch from a fresh `origin/main` (`git checkout --detach` the main checkout first, then `git worktree add --no-track -B <branch> ../objectstack-issue-27138 origin/main`); `pnpm install` (frozen lockfile); push with `git push -u origin <branch>` (⛔ no force).

Writes: PR only through the relay op `pr_create` (`node scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --actions-file F`, F a bare JSON array `[{"op":"pr_create","title":…,"head":"<your branch>","base":"main","body":…,"assignees":["os-warren"]}]`, draft forced; `--dry-run` first); your report comment through `node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs --comment=27138 --file=F --json` run ONCE with output captured to a file (no time-shaped stamp inside the fenced report JSON). ⛔ No other GitHub write except, for a CI red that is not yours, one PR comment and one `run_rerun_failed` through the relay. Report both counts (`api_writes` with endpoints, `mcp_calls` with tool names). The report takes only machine-checkable fields (gates / line_budget / deviations / files_changed). PR body: line 1 the platform attribution comment, line 3 `Fixes #27138`, then `## 维护者速读` six lines in Chinese (改了什么/为什么改/风险与回滚/先看/两分钟验证/需要你做的). Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on your diff, run each, record exits before any pipe, reconcile with `--ran` (merge `origin/main` first if it refuses as STALE TREE); `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` is a gate on every ui card. Build the closure your tests import first (`bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '<pkg>^...' build"`). Changeset in the root `.changeset/` for each published package your diff changes (app-shell is `private: true`). ⛔ `ui/.github/**` and the root `ci.yml` are out of bounds. Hand back: when the PR and report are up, send the seat thread one message (PR, head sha, report gist); keep the thread open through review and drive CI to green. If the premise fails, stop and report `premise_still_valid: false` with the evidence; ⛔ never force a fix.

### Ruling (cannot be re-ruled)

Ruling 6457467702 (#26594, letter B): the answer is the gate's own verdict, never a second client-side evaluator. Triage 6464880806: p2. ⛔ The dialog asks the server whether **this row** is writable, and does not re-derive sharing in the browser. The prerequisite #27175 landed as PR #27232 (`8bb2c31b`, 13:39Z). The record projection now carries `writable: boolean`. Seat note 6468378207 (spec seat 1) is part of this order: `writable` does **not** cover the approvals record lock, which has its own reader (`IApprovalService.getRecordLock`). A row under approval must also read that lock, or the dialog offers fields a save then refuses.

### PM mechanism assumptions (measure; disproof welcome)

On `origin/main` `0d45c0e7` (read-only check):
- `GetRecordFieldAccessResponseSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` ≈L3183) has `writable`. Its describe lists what `true` does not promise: the approval lock, conditional read-only and validation on the values sent, and so on.
- On the ui side, the type `RecordFieldAccess` (`ui/packages/types/src/data.ts` ≈L351) has no `writable`. `RecordFieldAccessAnswer` (`ui/packages/permissions/src/RecordFieldAccessScope.tsx` ≈L19) reads `editable` only. Check whether `ObjectStackAdapter.getRecordFieldAccess` (`ui/packages/data-objectstack`) passes the field through untouched.
- Two scopes mount the answer: `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/recordFieldAccess.tsx` (ModalForm, DrawerForm and ObjectForm edit) and, since #27146, `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/recordFieldAccess.tsx` (the detail page's inline edit).
- The approval lock already reaches the console through `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts` (`recordLock`, `recordLockedByApproval`). Measure how the record page's Edit action and inline edit read it today (#25934 precedent: 409 on a locked row), and whether the edit dialog reads it at all.

### PM suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

1. Carry `writable` through the type and adapter. In the scope, `writable: false` means every field on the record is not editable. Keep one source: the scope answers `usePermissions()` the same way it does for `editable`, so every gate below it (`gateFormFields`, `applyFieldPermissions`, `fieldWriteGate`, detail inline edit) reads it with no call-site change. An absent `writable` (an older server) changes nothing.
2. The dialog draws the record read-only with a short reason, and Save is not offered. Reuse an existing i18n key if one says "you can't edit this record"; otherwise add one key in every pack.
3. Approval lock: if the edit dialog and the record page's Edit action do not already read `getRecordLock` / `recordLock`, wire the existing reader in, without a second evaluator. If that needs app-shell to pass the lock into plugin-form, keep it a prop or context, not an import of app-shell. If it turns into its own surface, stop and report it as a finding instead of widening.

Tests: a `public_read` row the caller may read but not write (`writable: false`) opens the edit dialog read-only with no Save. CONTROL: `writable: true` with `editable` fields keeps them editable. CONTROL: no `writable` key behaves as before. The detail inline edit on `writable: false` offers no editor. Ablation: drop the `writable` read and the first test reds.

### Scope

File surface: `ui/packages/types/src/data.ts`; `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/**` only if the adapter strips the key; `ui/packages/permissions/src/**`; `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/{recordFieldAccess.tsx,ModalForm.tsx,DrawerForm.tsx}`; `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/recordFieldAccess.tsx`; the record page's Edit action call site in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/**` only for the approval-lock wiring; i18n packs for one key; tests beside them. Root `.changeset/` for every published package touched.

Serial: open PRs #27269 (spec seat, form buttons) and #27159's branch (seat 2, retiring split) both edit `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx`. ⛔ Stay out of `ObjectForm.tsx`, since the scope already mounts there through `recordFieldAccess.tsx`. No open PR touches the other files (open PR list read 2026-10-28T14:32Z).

### Tier

`TIER_DEFAULT`, effort `medium` (M). `Clause-②: no` (the renderer reads an answer the server already serves), `Metadata-protocol: none`.
